Q20 Q21
Slightly important I think the importance of this depends on the research questions/aims and the research field. In some areas it would be expected that there is a lot of remaining heterogeneity in the data, so reporting on it isn’t that informative. Perhaps something to include in a supplementary table.
Very important It should be mentioned in the text and detailed in supplimentary materials.
Extremely important Maybe add, ‘is is correctly described’ - they are often not correctly described.
Extremely important Reporting a measure of heterogeneity between effect size estimates in a meta-analysis is important because it allows other researchers to understand how much the effect sizes vary across the studies in the meta-analysis. This information is essential for interpreting the results of the meta-analysis.
Very important I think heterogeneity measures are commonly required for meta-analyses
Very important Understand more about the assumptions and limitations
Moderately important I am not so familiar with all of this - haven’t used it in my meta analysis…
Moderately important Not sure of my response. Q and I2 are not well understood and interpreted I think. Many people reading Meta-analyses do not focus on this. + In ecological studies the between study heterogeneity is often very very large. But, yes, it is mathematically important.
Very important Limitations an interpretation of heterogeneity tests should be discussed.
Extremely important Unsure what is meant by measure of heterogeneity. Also, perhaps measure of heterogeneity is not as important as the clarity on the method for estimating the heterogeneity, the size of heterogeneity and the correct interpretation of that value.
Extremely important The report of heterogeneity is important to correctly report and interpret data.
Extremely important very important for later decision making
Not at all important I assume heterogeneity by default so I’m just not that interested in testing for this. Put another way, if I’m going to use varying (aka random) effects in my model anyways because they’re more efficient (e.g. Andrew Gelman talks a lot about this), then the test is meaningless. According to some, testing for heterogeneity is important when interpreting ‘overall effects’ from meta-analyses; I can see that. But I’m also never interested in such ‘overall effects’ in many contexts as it’s akin to giving the weather forecast for a continent: effects are always conditional, and particularly for environmental sciences, those conditions arise from different studies. So I wouldn’t want to enforce such a test when it’s unnecessary.
Very important Could be useful to provide examples, like I2.
Very important This practice assesses consistency among studies, providing information about the agreement or variation of results. An appropriate measure of heterogeneity enhances the interpretation of results and the formulation of conclusions. It allows for the identification of potential confounding factors or moderators and demonstrates a rigorous and transparent methodological approach, essential for scientific credibility. Ideally, authors should report which measure was used and how it influences the interpretation of the meta-analysis results, thus strengthening the robustness and reliability of the study.
Extremely important fundamental to assess if meta-analysis is feasible and reliable.
NA So, by measure of heterogeneity, do you mean sd, se, range, 95%CI, etc.?
Very important Important for interpretation and assessment of bias
Very important Heterogeneity refers to the variability in effect sizes across different samples and is one of the major criteria to judge the importance and advancement of a scientific area.
Very important would be interesting to know what measure is reported
Moderately important I cannot answer this. I do not understand the question
Very important Some statistical tests assume the homogeneity between effect size estimates. So, the authors must let the readers know how they deal with the heterogeneity.

Q22 Q23
Extremely important It shouldn’t be published without this.
Moderately important Depended on the purpose of analysis, meta-regression may be carried out.
Very important Reporting the moderator variables included in a meta-regression in a meta-analysis is important because it allows other researchers to understand how the effect sizes vary depending on the characteristics of the studies. This information can be helpful for identifying the factors that influence the effect size and for developing theories about the underlying mechanisms.
Extremely important Part of the model description - if moderators are used, they also need to be reported.
Very important Understand the correlation of each variables
Moderately important Depend on the aim/objective of the study. It could only be estimate the mean effect, size, or calculate the homogeneity/heterogeneity between effectsize and identify the moderators. In some cases, yes, very important. (but we should also on how the moderators effects are estimated, meta-regression, meta-forest, …).
Extremely important Without reporting them, different meta-regressions could give different results, so of course this should be required.
Extremely important very important as testing the effect of these moderators is the point of conducting the meta-regression.
Extremely important Very important, otherwise the metaregression doesn’t have much utility to the reader.
Very important Whenever the data is available it is important to test for variables that could alter meta-analysis results or modulate data in a different direction/significance. But this should not be used to downgrade the quality of the meta-analysis if the authors disclose the lack of data for moderator variables use or high heterogeneity of studies included that prevents a moderator variables analysis.
Extremely important The only case I can imagine with NA making sense is a model with no moderators. It is quite rare but the option still exists, so I’d suggest to open up the possibility for an NA option
Extremely important Preferably these are specified in a protocol already or clear justification is made why these were selected. However, here I would like to have the option NA in case meta-regression wasn’t performed.
Extremely important Perhaps a bit tautological in that it is hard to imagine a scenario in which you wouldn’t do this
Moderately important Although rare, there may be small meta-analyses without moderators, which will make this question irrelevant. Here, inspecting figures and the results section could help know what moderator variables were used, although not specifically mentioned in the methods.
Moderately important Not all meta-analyses will have meta-regressions, so question should have an “if applicable”.
Extremely important Reporting on moderating variables in a meta-regression in a meta-analysis is crucial for the quality of the scientific report. This provides a detailed understanding of how moderating variables influence the relationships studied, significantly improving the interpretation of the results. It allows for the identification of specific conditions or groups where the effects are more pronounced. Transparency and methodological rigor in presenting these variables are essential for other researchers to assess the robustness of the analysis. Furthermore, the discussion on moderating variables can shed light on unexplored areas and guide future research. Authors should detail in the manuscript or supplementary material the selected moderating variables, their reasons for including them, and their expected impact on the results, thereby enriching the understanding and accumulation of knowledge in the field.
Extremely important Without knowing of moderator, meta-regression is not helpful
NA Not familiar with “moderator” variable – are you talking about fixed/random effects in a meta-regression model? Overall, it would be helpful to have definitions, examples, and citations to the language you’re using.
Extremely important More important than reporting moderators would be the reasoning behind why those moderators were tested
Extremely important Important for interpretation, assessment of bias and repeatability
Very important to evaluate the con-founders and moderators in our main Meta-analysis effects.
Extremely important Any items related to how the statistical analysis was done should be reported, especially when they can greatly influence the results.
Extremely important If, what you call ‘moderator variable’ is what I would call confounding variable or interactive variable, that this is the most important of all points. See my earlier comments. Your phrasing reads a bit cryptic to me.
Extremely important If a meta-regression is conducted it is of course extremely important to report the moderator variables, but that is not the same as saying that it is extremely important to conduct a meta-regression.
Extremely important I guess including moderator variables would be part of the hypothesis that are to be tested, so reporting these would be essential
Extremely important If moderators are included in a meta-regression, then yes, absolutely any and all moderators should be reported. These moderators should ALSO be clearly described/defined and include units/categories if applicable. For instance, although MATES item #16 captures whether authors report the data extracted from each eligible primary study, authors could make modifications or standardize this information prior to the actual analysis (e.g., convert information extracted as a continuous variable during the data extraction stage into a categorical variable for analysis). So not just did they report the moderators (Y/N) but do they also describe/define them. Your example captures the necessary information but the criteria could be refined to be more explicit about the description part possibly?

 kable(df_Q25, "html") %>%
    kable_styling("bordered", position = "left") %>%

Q24 Q25
Moderately important

In theory, I think this is important. But I don’t think it does its job. I’ve read a number of papers that state something like ‘we found evidence of publication bias, but we don’t think it’s much so we are just going to ignore it, cool, cool, cool’.

So, in reality, it doesn’t seem to change how authors, reviewers, editors or readers view the paper. That diminishes the importance of reporting it. There needs to be a clear expectation of what should be done when there is publication bias, and how papers with evidence of a publication bias should be framed and interpreted.
Very important This information is important for evaluating the results.
Moderately important People should consider them for sure, I am less impressed by the actual measures. I would say have they considered publication bias, with a test if appropriate.
Very important Reporting a sensitivity analysis in a meta-analysis is important because it allows other researchers to assess the robustness of the results to different assumptions and decisions. By reporting a sensitivity analysis, other researchers can be confident that the results of the meta-analysis are not simply due to the specific choices that were made in the analysis.
Slightly important Commonly done as part of the meta-analysis, but I am not sure how important it is. The tools available for testing publication bias are limited and not able to detect publication bias in many cases.
Very important Check the robustness of the study
Very important Yes, But not sufficient. If there is a publication biais. What do we do?? I would propose to better handle publication biais directly in the model(e.g. New method (e.g. robust bayesian meta-analysis;), and not analysing it after and say just yes/no. And I often do not totally trust the authors that say that there is no publication biais using visual analysis of funnel plot,….
Moderately important I think this is one aspect that many authors still struggle with, and I think better explanations of how to include this in common statistical packages are needed
Very important Consideration of publication bias is a key indicator of the quality of the review
Very important Limitations and interpretation of publication bias tests should be discussed. Funnel plot asymmetry and assoicated test can be due to other factors in addition to small sample size
Slightly important I don’t think this is very important as it is very difficult to assess publication bias with any degree of certainty. Surely all the information on the actual meta-analyses, the statistical models, the independence of studies etc is more of interest.
Extremely important To ensure validity of the meta-analysis
Extremely important Publication bias is a hughe problem, because non-significant resutls are rarely published, as well as results which do not match the scientists hypothesis.
Extremely important it should be methodology for publication bias and estimated size of bias.
Not at all important I’ve never been convinced this is a very valuable exercise. Publication bias surely exists, as does system selection, etc.
Extremely important Assuming this includes visual assessments
Extremely important Different studies with different methods are already a bias for a meta-analysis and the latter should be used in a set of studies with the best quality and not only the ones with the best results.
Moderately important i am not sure how well they generally work, but i guess better than nothing
Moderately important I did some meta-analyses where the variables that we were concerned with were just a few of dozens that were typically reported in the studies. They were rarely a principal item of interest to the authors of the original studies, and therefore it was implausible that the outcomes for these variables would have much influence on whether material was published- these were a set of studies that just pretty much reported a ton of stuff whether it showed a pattern or didn’t. So I never thought publication bias was much of an issue with these meta-analyses; I’d include them if reviewers were concerned, cause why not? So to some extent, perhaps with most or all the questions in this instrument, I think something like: “Do the authors report a test or measure of publication bias within the manuscript or supplementary material, or provide a clear explanation of why this was not done?” might be appropriate. All these steps shouldn’t just be taken without throught.
Very important The last time I checked, this is quite hard to achieve for models with moderators and non-independence
Extremely important this should also include a justification if this is not possible (e.g. small sample size)
Extremely important Does this mean that the answer will be “no” for articles reporting only a visual assessment of publication bias? It would be a good idea to clarify this point for future assessors.
Moderately important I view all research as biased in some way, we can’t help it, so publication bias is sneaking around in virtually any meta-analysis. But I also don’t think it’s that straightforward to suss out and funnel plots/Eggers tests can’t do it all. I’m mixed on this one… Suggest at least relaxing the “test or measure” part as it’s not that easily quantified; in its place, some effort to “discuss or acknowledge” the publication bias risk and its possible effect on the inferences of the meta-analysis (which is most important of all).
Extremely important Essential; no further comment.
Extremely important This activity is key to assessing the validity and reliability of the results, as publication bias can significantly alter conclusions. It provides transparency and demonstrates methodological rigor, allowing readers and other researchers to understand the potential limitations of the study. Addressing this bias increases confidence that the conclusions reflect a fair and unbiased synthesis of the evidence. Additionally, identifying publication bias may indicate the need for further research in potentially biased or incomplete areas. Authors should report the techniques used to assess this bias, such as funnel plots, Egger’s tests, or sensitivity analyses, in the manuscript or supplementary material. This practice not only improves the quality of the report but also strengthens the integrity and robustness of the research.
Moderately important Often a narrative discussion of this is more important, as the tests of PB are not the greatest. A lot of MA are really too small for any meaningful tests anyway. I would say ‘test or measure (if appropriate), or narrative discussion of…’
Extremely important At least of main analyses, not all sensitivity and stratified analyses.
Very important Important bias for the meta-analysis that should be considered
Very important is part of the critical evaluation process
Extremely important when studies with significant results are more likely to be published than non-significant findings – has dangerous consequences for meta-analyses.
Very important I think the ideal situation is that publication bias is reported. But, in my opinion, it is also valid to mention in the paper that the authors are aware of publication bias, and that the analysis is done on significant test results (which are most often reported), even if no formal bias analysis is conducted.
Very important

would seem important to report biases of single studies (e.g. confounding, measurement bias, etc.) and assess their influences on meta-estimates of association;

would also seem important to document if single studies assess non linearity of association before polling estimates of primary studies;

would also seem important to document unexplained inconsistency between estimates of association from different studies;
Extremely important Again, if this refers to biased data handling (e.g. not stratifying data by things like age of people, or nutrition of plants, or experimental conditions such as indoor vs outdoor etc.) this is key.
Very important Although it is important to report a test or measure of publication bias, it is as important to keep in mind that it is quite hard to test for publication bias and that all those measures may be interpreted in different ways.
Moderately important Publication bias provides additional information (and potentially interesting insights into trends in the literature). If such trends are present they should be included in the analyses (as with any other confounding variable that can influence the validity of the inferences).
Extremely important Yep, this too is important. I sometimes feel researchers include this but they don’t really understand or interpret the measure properly. In fairness, interpretation of many pub bias tests are inherently tricky. But there are new approaches/methods that help. So I guess the question is whether it is simply enough that they do something to test pub bias but should it be necessary that they also justify their choice of test or measure?

Q26 Q27
Moderately important I think this again depends on the research question and aims. If there is a clear reason to run a sensitivity analysis then yes, this should be reported. But I could imagine in some cases, this might not be needed.
Moderately important It may be described in supplimentary materials.
Moderately important This is so contextual, again I would probably say ‘have they considered the need for sensitivity analyses and reported if necessary’
Extremely important Reporting the total number of studies included in the meta-analysis is important because it allows readers to assess the comprehensiveness of the review and the size of the evidence base. This information is also essential for assessing the generalizability of the findings.
Moderately important it depends on the case, if there are several possible outliers it becomes important
Very important Important to check which factors influence the results most
Very important Check the robustness of the model/parameters
Very important

For me sensitivity analysis are totally different from publication bias.

sensitivity analysis are for testing the hypothesis of the model structure, impact of missing data, type of inference (bayesian/frequentists), …. If the authors do not present sensitivity analysis, I could consider it as a kind of p-hacking, perhaps involving debatable model choices
Slightly important Same comments as the last question
Moderately important This may not be applicable to all reviews but is important to include where relevant
Extremely important If it applicable, then should be reported. Otherwise, no.
Extremely important Sensitivity analyses, to me ,is more important than publication bias test
Moderately important I think this makes much more sense than the publication bias tests. But it depends on the context so it is not motivated in all cases.
Extremely important Formualtion of the question could be clearer “report a sensitivity analysis” or perhaps “report details of methods for and outcomes of sensitivity analysis”.
Slightly important Depends on the data and if there are indications a small number of studies might be mighty influential
Extremely important This and the bias measure are both essential parts of the theory of meta-analysis. Most of the things which have gone before are more broadly applicable to statistical projects, but this gets to the core of what meta-analysis tries to do by synthesising studies.
Extremely important The sensitivity analysis is important to test for the reliability of the obtained results.
Slightly important sensitivity to what? too vague…
Extremely important With the provisos indicated for other questions
Very important I am not sure what this means ‘sensitivity analysis’ - sensitivity of what? this could be important or not important at all depending on the definition of this
Moderately important In a way, ‘sensitivity’ is addressed by measures such as cross-validation, it just may not be labelled as such. In any case, ‘sensitivity analysis’ needs to be clarified for what specific part of the meta-analysis (the dataset, the statistical model, other inputs, the literature search itself even) this applies to.
Very important I am confused why the item refers to “sensitivity analysis IN ADDITION to a publication bias test”. These are often very different tests, and should be considered separately.
Slightly important Doesn’t necessarily apply to all meta-analyses, so should have an “if applicable”.
Very important Conducting and reporting a sensitivity analysis in a meta-analysis is essential for the quality of the scientific report. This analysis assesses the robustness of the results against variations in methods, assumptions, or study inclusion criteria, providing a crucial measure of the soundness of the conclusions. It helps identify potential sources of bias or variability, thereby improving the credibility and transparency of the study. Furthermore, the findings from a sensitivity analysis can guide future research by highlighting areas of significant impact on the results. Authors should report this analysis along with tests for publication bias, detailing their methodology and its influence on the overall interpretation of the meta-analysis. This practice not only improves the quality of the report but also strengthens confidence in the validity and robustness of the study’s findings.
Very important If appropriate
Extremely important In meta-analysis, different estimate method may produce largely different results.
Slightly important Do all meta-analyses conduct sensitivity analyses? My guess is maybe not. So, if they didn’t conduct one and therefore didn’t report it, then does that count against them in some way?
Very important The reason I chose very important,and not extremely important, is that I haven’t conducted sensitivity analysis in my meta-analysis. From those I read, the presence of sensitivity analysis felt like a plus. An important plus, absolutely. But seeing that most reviews don’t consider or include some basic steps in the systematic review and meta-analysis, sensitivity analysis is very important but it do not seem crucial.
Not at all important This lends itself to assessing the bias of the meta-analysis, not the reporting as such as it relates to the conduct of the analysis. Important to distinguish.
Moderately important if ther eis sensitivity it is important. This is not always the case
Very important A sensitivity analysis is usually included in a meta-analysis because of uncertainty regarding the effectiveness or safety of an intervention. Sensitivity analyses are purposed to gain insight and certainty about the validity of research findings reported.
Very important i would be more specific and ask whether authors assessed the influence of residual confounding or biases on the meta-estimate
Extremely important sure you want to see the power of the analysis, for instance how sensitive the analysis is with regard to the inclusion or exclusion of certain criteria by which the data were stratified (sorted)
Very important Here you may want to be a bit more specific about what the sensitivity analysis should be based on (e.g., critical appraisal assessment or other subgroups). Also, do you include for example fail-safe number analysis to test robustness here?
Extremely important Sensitivity analyses provide valuable information because even the most detailed meta-analysis can let outside other sources of information. So, knowing which results are less or more sensitive to excluding information is crucial.
Moderately important In answering this question I am a little biased, because in a recent meta-analysis we tried to use the critical appraisal tool for study validity assessment proposed by Konno et al (2021) and that did not work out too well – the tool was not very well fitted to the ecological field studies we were assessing, so reviewers using the tool were not very consistent in their assessment

Very important It provides a framework for interpreting the results. More important is publishing the data somewhere.
Extremely important Absolutely important information.
Extremely important Basic information, must include this.
Very important This is important so that the reader knows to which extend data was available - Not sure how study is defined here - Can one study include several effect sizes? Should be specified.
Very important Understand the sampling size
Moderately important I would tend to focus more on the accuracy of the estimated effects (i.e., mean effect, confidence intervals, heterogeneity, etc.). For me, the number of included studies is often a “headline effect”, to get published in ‘big’ journals. + we could extract several effect-sizes for une primary study.. But important to clearly have the list of studies and the database , for transparency, reproducibility, and to update the database
Extremely important There should be a list of all studies, not only the total number. I have bene involved in instances were a different research group have tried to replicate a meta-analysis done by another group, and without the study lists it would be difficult to determine why both groups got completely different results
Extremely important This is a fundamental piece of information for the methods of a systematic review. Ideally the full references of every included study should also be available.
Extremely important This is a key element.
Extremely important It is important to discuss criteria for selection of studies and selection of risk estimates. Also meta-analysis should not be done on small numbers of studies
Extremely important Very fundamental information that simply must be there.
Extremely important a very basic information needed to give an idea of the comprehensiveness of the search and available studies.
Extremely important Pivotal to the quality of reporting so the reader knows the breadth of studies in the analyses
Extremely important It’s important that you clarify what is meant by study. I find this is a chronic source of confusion. It it a paper? An experiment? An effect size? Something else?
Very important It helps readers contextualise the synthesis in terms of the knowledge base.
Extremely important The higher the number the higher the strengh of the meta-analysis and this is a basic reporting that needs to be disclose in every review
Extremely important Essential. No further comment.
Extremely important Reporting the total number of studies in a meta-analysis is vital for the quality of the scientific report. This information provides insight into the breadth and representativeness of the evidence reviewed, which is crucial for assessing the reliability of the results. A larger number of studies generally implies greater statistical power and reliability. Transparency in presenting this number reflects a rigorous and methodical approach in the research, essential for the integrity of the study. Additionally, it facilitates reproducibility and verification of the analysis by other researchers. Authors should clearly detail the total number of studies and the selection process in the manuscript and supplementary material, allowing for a thorough and critical evaluation by the scientific community and reinforcing the robustness of the meta-analysis.
Extremely important Mandatory to evaluate what studies are assessed and included compared to those not.
Extremely important Important for interpretation and repeatability
Very important Useful for defining the research question, data collection, data preparation, data analysis, and reporting and meta-analysis.
Extremely important This is basic information and should be included. Analyzing 3 vs. 35 papers will have different implications for statistics and robustness.
Extremely important is it really a question to ask - would anyone perform a meta-analysis without reporting the n?
Extremely important Trivial, of course you need to describe your sample and what its structure is
Extremely important This is related to the previous question. The readers need to know how many studies were included in the meta-analysis because slight differences in the number of studies can lead to distinct results if the sensitivity is high.
Extremely important Again, this goes back to the transparency of reporting :)
Extremely important I think it is also important to define what they used as a ‘study’. Sometimes the study could be the primary paper itself, but sometimes there could be multiple case studies reported in a single primary paper (which in turn is still different from an effect size, as multiple effect sizes could be reported from a single case study e.g., different species outcomes). So, do they report the total number of studies included in the analysis and define a study.

NA I am not sure to totally understand the question. Do the authors present a forest plot, or other type of plot? Yes, important to better communicate the results. Slightly important could tables and figures be explicitly described here? would there be examples so that the appraiser knows what this mean

Moderately important A figure will simplify the message for easier and faster understanding, but not that crucial as long as the results were part of the text

Moderately important It can be helpful but isn’t strictly neccessary
Extremely important Extremely important to the reader to verify if the interpretation of the authors are correct.
Moderately important summary statistics in the text can be sufficient for simple analyses of mean effects, but visualization nice to ensure patterns arent driven by outliers
NA I honestly didn’t understand the question “Do the authors report the results using a visualisation in the manuscript or supplementary material?” when I read it first in your spreadsheet. But now I am thinking the question means “Did they use figures to report the results.” Or maybe that’s not what this means? I would generally expect there to be figures, but perhaps if there wasn’t there was a reason? (honestly, I’d just be very surprised!)
Extremely important It might be hard to understand for some people what a data visualisation is, but it is very important to allow checking how the data are distributed across the ranges/levels of moderators
Moderately important I think we are used to seeing results presented in visual formats and they do add value, e.g. in terms of distribution of effect sizes and CIs plus might show interesting patterns that wouldn’t be easy to pick up solely from text.
Slightly important as long as results are presented clearly, the way of presenting does not matter
Moderately important If the appropriate summary statistics are given, then of course this is not necessary, but it is extremely useful to get a general picture of the results quickly
Slightly important As long as the results are reported (in the form of text or using a visualisation) I think that’s fine
Extremely important I could understand why people would not rate this as “extremely important” because if people report e.g., the mean, confidence intervals, and heterogeneity, then most of the results are already presented. Very important No additional comment.

These tools make findings accessible to a broader audience, facilitating interpretation for both specialists and non-specialists alike. They are also useful for revealing trends, correlations, and anomalies in the data. The inclusion of visualizations demonstrates transparency and improves the reader’s experience, allowing for a more direct and profound understanding of the study’s findings. Therefore, it is ideal for authors to include such visualizations in the manuscript and supplementary material.
Extremely important It makes it easier to understand. A figure is easier to read than a table or text.
Extremely important Data in figures are very easy to read compared to tables.
Moderately important Again, define what you mean by visualization. Does that include tables? Or are you just talking about figures?

Moderately important it is useful, and make sthe data more insightful. It is not crucial for the quality or interpretation as such.
Very important Visualization helps us see the story the data is telling, enabling highly effective reporting practices.
Slightly important We usually use forest plots.
Slightly important Having text and plots makes a paper more digestable, but I don’t think this is crucial for the overall quality.
Moderately important nice to have, but if it hides or masks things because of two dimensional description of what is multidimensional they can also disguise the reality
Extremely important At least for me, a visual presentation of the obtained results is easy to understand and compare.
Very important Visualization tools are always helpful :)
Very important

Definitely very helpful to include visualizations of results but at minimum results of analyses should be described in text/tables.

Slightly important This is important for the context of open research and helping future researchers and also allows source data to be checked.
Moderately important sometimes you can not report the all extracted data, due to some limitation. But details of search strategy must be report with details.
Extremely important Very important for the possibility to reproduce or verify the analysis.
Extremely important Definitely! For reproducibility of the research, for open science
Extremely important Extremely important to know what actual data (which response traits) were extracted from each study.
Extremely important It’s relatively common to provide effect sizes. I think it is much more valuable to report the data used to obtain the effect size.
Very important Again general reproducibility.
Extremely important The data extraction is the basis for the begging of data retrieval and needs to be carefully conducted to enable the correct choice of variables and methods to be used in the meta-analysis.
Extremely important I mean, why not, but then again, do journals ask for all your data for all published primary articles?
Moderately important ’-Might very be hard to do if the authors have requested data to the authors of individual studies and there is potential conflict in terms of authorship/ data ownewship -The question should be more straight-forward: “What is the importance of publishing the database for the meta-analysis”? or similar. It is confusing to read “report the data extracted from each eligible primary study” -The yes and no responses include question marks, which they shouldn’t
Very important In general, data should be available.
Very important Not entirely clear in this wording if it refers to simply reporting what variables are extracted in a methods sense, or if it means depositing the raw data somewhere, or even if reproducible image extraction tools etc. Some clarification would be good here.
Extremely important I think it’s also important to report effect size estimates with the data extracted
Extremely important I’m very glad to see this item. It’s so disappointing how rare meta-analyses in my field actually include data! And it’s not even the authors’ data, it’s someone else’s! And it’s usually paid for by public funds, so it shouldn’t belong to any one individual! I’m hoping this helps things.
Extremely important Absolutely essential. Should also be provided in raw (i.e., direct from manuscript in original format) and harmonised formats, if possible.
Extremely important failure to report the data is discussing a paper which has no results section. The secondary data upon which the analysis is done is extremely important
Very important This ensures transparency and allows for the reproducibility of the analysis, fundamental elements for the integrity of scientific research. Providing details about the extracted data, such as sample size and outcome measures, enables readers and other researchers to evaluate the quality and relevance of the included studies. It facilitates detailed scrutiny and constructive criticism, thereby contributing to continuous improvement in the research field. Moreover, the availability of this data is invaluable for future research, providing a solid foundation for new studies. Therefore, it is ideal for authors to detail these data in the manuscript, supplementary material, or an external repository, which enriches the transparency and usefulness of the meta-analysis for the scientific community.
Very important A list may be enough, considering that is generally similar across reviews, but such brief list should be mandatory, extensive list is fine for supplementary material
Extremely important Important to guarantee transparency and reproducibility
Extremely important Important for assessing potential bias, interpretation and repeatability
Very important Extracting data from studies is the norm in meta-analyses, enabling researchers to generate effect sizes when raw data are otherwise not available.
NA It seems better to distinguish primary and secondary data extracted.
Moderately important Good for transparency and reproducibility, but not crucial for the overall quality.
Extremely important you mean descriptive stats upfront? The raw tables with what had been entered into the analysis must be reported in supplementary archives. That archive should already structured in a way how the data were used in the analysis.
Extremely important If anyone wants to reproduce the meta-analysis, sharing the original sources and the raw database is extremely important.
Moderately important I find it useful to include this information as supplementary materials

# Separate rows and count total for Question 36

  filter(!is.na(Q36)) %>%
  count(Q36) %>% 
  arrange(desc(n))

# Plot for survey question 36
fig_Q36 <-  total_data_description_report_count %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = reorder(Q36, n)), hjust = 0.5) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +

 geom_text(data = total_data_description_report_percentage, aes(label = paste0("(", round(percentage, 1), "%)"), x = n), 
            hjust = -0.1, size = 8, color = "black", fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_identity(guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0), limits = c(0, max(total_data_description_report_count$n*1.3))) +
  MATES_theme() +
  labs(caption = "MATES item 17\nThe value in each bar is the total number of participants")

PRISMA graph and a PICO, as it contains the search terms, the planned statistics and variables, with the results of each sorting phase
A few thoughts: - perhaps some criteria around the literature search should be included? E.g. does the study state the literature selection criteria, search terms, literature databases used, inclusion/exclusion criteria - clear definitions/criteria of treatment vs control groups? - choice of effect size (e.g. SMD) and justification? - a clear statement of any random effects and nesting of random effects?

Conflicts of interest: Reporting of conflicts of interest is important for assessing the credibility of the meta-analysis.

Funding sources: Reporting of funding sources is important for assessing the potential for bias in the meta-analysis

Protocol registration: Registration of the meta-analysis protocol is important for reducing the risk of bias

The MATES only focuse on the statistical procedure. A key requisite is having a clear and reasonable proposal, including research question, search strategy, inclusion and excusion criteria, etc.
None
A very important part of systematic reviews is the critical appraisal of each datapoint used for analysis. Quality criterial need to be defined and each data point should be subjected to those criteria. Authors need to describe how they deal with data points that were rated as problematic in one or more criteria. Such data points could either be excluded altogether, or sensitivity analyses could be performed to check if problematic data points change the result of the analysis. I think the evaluation of the critical appraisal is an important part of the reporting quality.
  1. Data transparency
  2. Step-by-step flow methodology
  3. Stakeholders engagement
Search strings + scientific Databases used + Kappa test + protocol + conflict of interest + …
Your survey was thorough. Maybe one thing that I try to remind my students to include in their meta-analysis manuscripts is the effect size interpretation to make sure that the reader understands what the results mean.
Justification for inclusion of different fixed an random effects. Justification for final model selection (if this is not already included in the question about the first model used)
I am surprised there is not mention of listing of search terms used and research databases used for global meta-analyses.
would specific definition of outcome and exposure matter too? or is it covered somewhere? comparable definitions and statement of possible bias from outcome and exposure measurements is crucial to be described for each study
Apart from publication bias, I think publication year is also important.
Perhaps also if there is a visualisation of the data across the different moderators/species etc so that the reader can see how the data is distributed and how different data points are related
Report of search strategy in any database in detail. Any transformation performed on the variables. How the handling with cross over trials and when some results published in tow or more published paper?
Criteria for selecting studies, criteria for selecting effect estimates from studies (e.g. many studies report several estimates).
study quality evaluation and bias analyses, including direction and magnitude of the bias . Bias should be consider in exploring sources of heterogeneity.
It seems pretty comprehensive to me, based on my book learning about how to do meta-analysis.
The focus is currently very much on classical meta-analysis, and is therefore not necessarily applicable to other forms of synthesis, such as the re-analysis of raw data. Unsure how can I access the complete set of MATES questions…

Database availability. Without complete database it is not possible to evaluate the quality of meta-analysis, or repeat the same meta-analysis, or enlarge the current database after some years.
Perhaps an explanation of the choice of measure of effect size.
It is important to report if the methods used were based on guidelines already available and revised by competent entities.
Selection criteria of primary studies; language of primary studies considered
I see that you are interested in the analytical part of the meta-analysis, but I think that the characteristics of the literature search and selection criteria can also affect the quality of the meta-analysis and often these are not clearly reported.
I’m surprised you didn’t mention inclusion criteria. What defined whether data were included in the meta-analysis? In my experience, often the inclusion criteria of the systematic review are broader than those that define the studies entering the meta-analysis.

I might also be tempted to report how many studies collected useful data but the data were not retrievable (either data not open access or author did not respond to email) or usable (missing standard errors).

any conversions/harmonizations done e.g., whether only max and mins could be retrieved and the meta-analysis used these to calculate a mean to align with the means retrieved from other studies.

Something maybe also about justification of effect size metric and scale/units?

And whether moderator variables were extracted from the original papers or rather extracted from elsewhere by the person doing the meta-analysis. Seems relevant for accountability of the analysis. I would probably trust moderator variables from the original papers more.
I think the survey is complete, just maybe the importance of the language for search strategies, which should be considered and explained in manuscript.
Perhaps this is covered elsewhere in the reporting framework but it is generally useful to know the study retrieval process and screening and selection criteria for studies included in the MA. Also useful to report relevant measures of statistical fit of the MA model and predictive performance (if the MA model is used for in-sample or out-of-sample prediction).
So far there is no question on the reporting of results except on heterogeneity. Probably there are many aspects to consider about the results
Can’t think of any if MATES is used together with another appraisal tool that considers consistency in data extraction etc.
are aims and objectives of the meta-analysis clearly defined
Maybe these are viewed as more the systematic review process than the meta-analysis per se, but search terms and strategies, data extraction processes, interrater reliability, some sort of PRISMA flow diagram, .

I think another key element is the reporting on how the data was extracted from studies (the method, software/packages used to extract data from figures for example, etc.)

Also, the way in which the articles were searched, screened, etc. to form the final database are also key stages in the meta-analysis and must be well reported.
This isn’t that directly quantifiable, but I believe a statement supporting what context(s) the meta-analysis really pertains to would be good. For example, a meta-analysis might be labelled as “global” (this is very common in my field) which actually means, the allowable sources of literature was global in scope. The actual data collected is very often not global – e.g. studies might be concentrated in N. America, Europe, maybe Oceania, maybe some in Asia, but not at all in Africa. My opinion is that “global” is misleading here. What would be better would be to describe what conditions the meta-analysis really cover. For example, if studying responses across major soil orders of the world, report that “of the 32 world reference soil groups, the dataset compiled here represents 18 soil groups (Table X)”. Relatedly, an assessment of exchangeability in observations is critical in my opinion. This is in context of multilevel models – A. Gelman talks a bit about this, as does Richard McElreath. An example of the discussion of this issue in my general field is this paper by Eagle et al. (doi: 10.2134/agronj2017.04.0215). In other words, the observations being compared shouldn’t be apples v. oranges.
As I’ve noted elsewhere, it is critical for meta-analyses to report on harmonisation of data given the heterogeneity in study designs and reporting.
There are no criteria to assess the reporting quality on article selection and the review process which are two important steps in developing a meta-analysis. I am not sure whether this tool is limited to the data analysis process. However, if the tool is developed to assess the reporting quality of a meta-analysis, it would be worth to include criteria to assess the article selection and review process as well.
My reservation is on extraction of the secondary data and ensuring that it is comprehensive. Full disclosure of databases consulted and ranges are crucial.
To include the codes of data analysis.
The amount of data for each outcome in the subgroup meta-analysis should be given.
Datasets characteristics used in the studies, as the environmental field has different datasets that are related to time ( when the data is gathered and for how long)
Research question (PECO), tool fo risk of bias?, literature strategies, inclusion/exclusion criteria
Share the dataset and code used to increase confidence in them.

How the data are extracted (e.g. by whom, how differences addressed); appraisal of the included studies (who, how). PRISMA guidelines are really useful for this.
The calculations are spoton and the images are sharp enough for use in publication.

There are other suggestions that I can present if you contact me.
May be beyond the scope of this, but it is valuable to assess whether studies included in a meta-analysis were quality checked (bad data in, bad data out…..). If a meta-analysis actually quality checked the studies it is based on, it could hint at the overall quality of the meta-analysis as well.
The most important thing happens before meta-analysis. I saw only biased meta-analysis because this data handling was left to software and stats people. The sorting of data and the specification of co-variables and interactive terms must be decided by the best experts of the subject. Possible by a consortium of experts. The technical part that follows is of secondary importance.
  1. Funding information of the meta-analyses;
  2. Risk of bias assessment

  4. Non-linear pooling, if possible
Appropriate methods for number of studies / effect sizes included
You did a very detailed job and included all the necessary elements to assess the quality of the meta-analysis.

Question 4

Provide feedback and suggest rewording of the following item (if necessary):

Referring to MATES item 2:

MATES item 2: Code reporting

Question

o Do the authors report any relevant code used to conduct the analysis (i.e., the code used to conduct the computations, statistical models, and inferences comprising the meta-analysis) in the manuscript, supplementary material, or external repository?

Criteria for ‘Yes’

o The authors have reported any relevant code used to conduct the analysis in the manuscript, supplementary material, or external repository.

Criteria for ‘No’

o The authors have not reported any relevant code used to conduct the analysis in the manuscript, supplementary material, or external repository.

Criteria for ‘Not Applicable’

o The authors have used a GUI/click based software that does not produce a code or syntax. Alternatively, the authors have not reported the software used to conduct the analysis (i.e., ‘No’ to MATES item 1).

  • The information provided in the glossary - definition of the graphical user interface (GUI) - was essential in order to be able to respond correctly if software such as Stata was used.

Extremely easy NA

This distinction was mostly clear to me after reading the MATES checklist and glossary, so perhaps some of that text could be included for the ‘Not Applicable’ category.
Extremely easy I don’t agree with the NA. Code is either there or not, and for full transparency it should be. Using a GUI does not mitigate that lack of transparency.
Somewhat difficult This was difficult to apply to studies which used a GUI which could provide a syntax or coding log but this has not been reported in the manuscript or SI. Extremely easy NA

Somewhat easy It may be hard for some people to decide between “No” and “NA”, because it requires knowledge on which software uses code vs. point-and-click.
Somewhat easy Good question to evaluate the transparency and reproducibility of studies. But very rarely done.

Question 6

Question

Criteria for ‘Not Applicable’

Question 12

MATES item 6: Model type reporting

Question

o Do the authors report the type of the meta-analytic/meta-regression model (e.g., fixed, random, or multi-level models), either descriptively or in statistical notation in the manuscript or supplementary material?

Criteria for ‘Yes’

o The authors have reported the type of the meta-analytic/meta-regression model, either descriptively or in statistical notation in the manuscript or supplementary material.

Criteria for ‘No’

o The authors have not reported the type of the meta-analytic/meta-regression model, either descriptively or in statistical notation in the manuscript or supplementary material.

Criteria for ‘Not Applicable’

o There is no ‘Not Applicable’ option for MATES item 6.

Q13 Q12
Somewhat easy Unclear what you mean by “structure” - may need to explain that this means more than just stating that it was “random” or “fixed”?
NA NA
Extremely easy NA
Extremely easy NA
Extremely easy To be able to answer yes, does the model have to be specified (for example, in case of a random model how is the random part structured?) or is simply mentioning the type of model (fixed, random, …) sufficient?
Somewhat difficult Similar to #5, it was often hard to find this information.
Somewhat easy The studies I reviewed varied widely in terms of the amount of detail provided for this item. I eventually decided to say ‘Yes’ if authors provide ANY mention of this, even if it is sometimes just a short sentence (e.g. “We used a random effects model.”). This is a bit ambiguous though, and it is possible that some other MATES participants may disagree.
Somewhat easy NA
Somewhat easy NA
Somewhat easy NA
Somewhat easy Keywords like fixed, random, or multi-level model are used to search.
Somewhat easy The authors almost always report the type of model they use, but the details of the model specifications are often unclear. For instance, some authors would state that they used a “random-effect model” only when “they found heterogeneity”. Identifying which model is fixed or random is thus unclear and not transparent. It is also almost always unclear what random effect is used. I get that the definition of a “random-effect” model is clear for most people (i.e., study-level random effect), but I think this item would be more interesting if authors clearly reported which random effects were used, particularly for multi-level models.
Neither easy nor difficult See my previous remark. Saying that a random-effects model was used is not enough in my opinion; more details are needed (especially about the structure of the random model, etc.)
Neither easy nor difficult NA
Somewhat easy NA

Question 14

Provide feedback and suggest rewording of the following item (if necessary):

Referring to MATES item 7:

MATES item 7: Effect size weights reporting

Question

o Do the authors report the sampling variance, sampling error or equivalent (i.e., strategy to assign weights) of effect size estimates in the manuscript or supplementary material?

Criteria for ‘Yes’

o The authors have reported the sampling variance, sampling error or equivalent of effect size estimates in the manuscript or supplementary material.

Criteria for ‘No’

o The authors have not reported the sampling variance, sampling error or equivalent of effect size estimates in the manuscript or supplementary material.

Criteria for ‘Not Applicable’

o The authors have conducted a meta-analysis without weights (i.e., unweighted meta-analysis).

    scroll_box(width = "150%", height = "400px")
Q15 Q14
Somewhat easy Change the order of wuation parts to make it clearer and align with other: “Do the authors report the strategy used to assign weights of effect size estimates (e.g. the sampling variance, sampling error or equivalent), in the manuscript or supplementary material?”
NA NA
Extremely easy NA
Somewhat easy NA
Somewhat easy Perhaps you should specify that the values are expected, because the weights can be reported graphically by differences in point size.
Extremely difficult This was quite confusing for me, especially the “No” versus “NA”. I really couldn’t tell the difference between these and when to select one over the other.
Somewhat easy I assumed this item was looking for authors to say something like “we weighted effect sizes based on the inverse of their sampling variances”, rather than provide the actual weights in a data file. However, I feel the way this item is written could be interpreted either way - perhaps re-word it so that the “strategy to assign weights” is emphasized first, instead of “reporting the sampling variance.”
Somewhat easy NA
Extremely difficult I found this criteria difficult to apply. This is either because none of the meta-analyses I reviewed reported the sampling variance, sampling error or equivalent, OR because I did not understand what would satisfy this criteria.
Somewhat easy I considered that 95%CI associated with effect sizes (reported in the text or shown in forest plots) would be a measure of weight
Somewhat easy NA
Somewhat difficult I was a bit confused about the wording of this item. It is quite common for authors to report the % of weights taken by each study in their analyses, but not how these weights were calculated, or even how the sampling variance of the effect size was calculated. Also, what if authors say they used an “inverse-variance model”, but do not provide the formula for calculating the sampling variance? How about cases where authors say they used a specific package (e.g., metafor) that automatically calculates sampling variance? I think this question needs to be very specific about what counts as “yes” or “no”.
Neither easy nor difficult The question may not be very clear. Do we want to know if and how the authors weighted the studies (and therefore that the text states this clearly), or do we want information on the precision of individual effect sizes?
Neither easy nor difficult Some papers seemed to be weighted in the results, although the authors did not explicitly state this
Somewhat easy NA

Question 16

Provide feedback and suggest rewording of the following item (if necessary):

Referring to MATES item 8:

MATES item 8: Effect size dependence (non-independence) reporting

Question

o Do the authors report the dependence (e.g., multiplicity or, repeated measure) of effect size estimates (e.g., acknowledge multiple effect sizes were taken from a single study) in the manuscript or supplementary material?

Criteria for ‘Yes’

o The authors have reported whether there is dependence of effect size estimates in the manuscript or supplementary material. If a meta-analysis reports that effect size estimates are independent allocate ‘Yes’.

Criteria for ‘No’

o The authors have not reported whether there is dependence of effect size estimates in the manuscript or supplementary material.

Criteria for ‘Not Applicable’

o There is no ‘Not Applicable’ option for MATES item 8.

Q17 Q16
Somewhat easy Sometimes they explicitly state they assume they are independent even they know they are not - not clear if this means that “If a meta-analysis reports that effect size estimates are independent” or not
NA NA
Extremely easy NA
Extremely easy NA
Somewhat easy How to respond when independence is not explicitly stated but is obvious (because one effect size = one primary study)?
Extremely difficult Authors don’t really seem to report this, so a lot of time is spent reading the paper and supplement trying to find out if this was done anywhere.
Somewhat difficult This is the item I had the most trouble with, especially because I found it difficult to separate from the item about model structure/random effects. Most studies that I reviewed used a random effects analysis, presumably to to deal with non-independence of effect sizes. I do understand the importance of explicitly recognizing non-independence in the text, but I think this item needs to be re-worded to some extent.
Neither easy nor difficult Are we only expecting this if there is a risk of non-dependency? A MA with say 6 studies with 6 author groups at 6 different times may not see the need to state this.
Extremely difficult I found this criteria difficult to apply. Similarly to MATES Item 7, I am unsure whether this is because none of the meta-analyses I reviewed included the dependence of effect size estimates OR because I wasn’t sure what would satisfy this criteria.
Somewhat easy I considered that a study would did not ‘report the dependence of effect size estimates’ when it did not state that explicitly in the text. However it is quite easy to see if there is dependency of effect sizes from the diference in the number of studies and the number of effect sizes, or from the repetition of a study reference in a forest plot. Therefore, the item would probably be better stated as ‘Do the authors ACKNOWLEDGE the dependence (e.g., multiplicity or, repeated measure) of effect size estimates…’
Neither easy nor difficult NA
Somewhat difficult This was a tricky one too. If the authors used a random-effect model, then in almost all cases it is to account for the non-independence of effect sizes among studies, but the authors do not necessarily mention non-independence directly. Also, what about cases when authors say that they extracted multiple effect sizes per study, but don’t do anything about it? Or what if they say that they used a random-effect model because they extracted multiple effect sizes per study, but don’t say that this generates a source of non-independence? I think it would be relevant to require people to statistically account for effect size dependence, not just “mention” non-independence.
Neither easy nor difficult Good question, but should we evaluate the strategies used by the authors? Pooling, exclusion, … Some are recommended, others are not…
Neither easy nor difficult NA
Somewhat easy NA

Question 30

Provide overall comments on MATES (e.g. order of questions, structure of questions or on glossary of terms)

# Filter for task question 30

  select(Q30)

# Table for task question 30
 kable(dat_task_Q30, "html") %>%
    kable_styling("bordered", position = "left") %>%
    scroll_box(width = "150%", height = "400px")
Q30
NA
NA
Overall easy to follow, but some items left room for some uncertainty
the tool is very well done, I don’t have particular comments on how to improve it, the various items are clearly described and it is easy to understant the various points. I furthermore think that the needed aspects of a meta-analysis were properly included in MATES
Suggested order of questions (to better follow the flow of article reading): 5 - 6 - 8 - 1 - 2 - 3 - 4 - 9 - 7 - 10 - 11 - 12 - 13 - 14
I wish I would have been able to answer the questions in whatever order I wanted to. I often found the information for items 10, 11, 12, 13 before items 6-9. Having to do them in a strict order made it take me longer than it would have otherwise.
I think this tool has immense promise overall - great work so far. However, some questions may need to be re-worded or have additional information added to aid users. Some explicit discussions with the larger MATES group about resolving ambiguity might also be helpful (e.g. exactly how much information needs to be reported to get a ‘yes’?).
Just a few suggestions. A lot of the latter information (ES, weighting, raw data etc.) should be in a forest plot. In healthcare it would be rare for a MA not to have a forest plot.

The questions could be presented in a different order e.g. I found that usually the first answer to appear in the text was referencing MATES Item 3 (number of primary studies), not the software used.

Should the date of literature searches also be reported for gold-standard? e.g. ‘Literature searches were conducted in May 2024’?

I found MATES item 7 and 8 consistently difficult and am not confident in my responses for these criteria.

I think the studies included should be referenced (e.g. a reference list in the Supplementary material) alongside the total number included?

A comprehensive description of the variables extracted could possibly include a unit where applicable?
Maybe rethink the phrasing of item 4 to focus on the number of effect sizes per subgroup instead of ‘total number of effect size estimates’ - for results interpretation it is more relevante to know the subgroup sample size than the total sample size. Maybe rethink the phrasing of item 8 to ‘Do the authors acknowledge the dependence…’ if the focus is to be on authors being aware of the implications of using multiple effect sizes per study. Maybe item 14 can also be made clear. I assumed that any list or table with moderators would qualify, but took me some time to process this item…
  1. Can provide suggestions on what kind of common keywords can be used for the question search.
  2. Provide some guidelines to the users where can we normally find the relevant answers. For example, authors tend to provide sensitivity analysis and publication bias in the supplementary materials.
I think the tool is pretty easy to use overall, but it would be helpful to have more examples or a small FAQ for each question. The description of each item is quite short and it leaves some gaps for interpretation. For instance, items 10-12 say that authors have to “report” publication bias/heterogeneity/sensitivity analyses. What if the authors say they did, but don’t report the results of these assessments? What if the authors’ objective is not to calculate an overall effect because it hardly makes sense for their study in Item 9? I really think a more thorough description of each item + a FAQ could help answer most questions people would have, and ensure the tool is fully reproducible. I also think that Item 6 is too vague, because the type of model does not tell much about the actual model structure. At the end of the day, I see this tool not just as an assessment of already published studies, but also as a guide people can use to design and report their study. If people see that only suggesting the model type is proposed in this tool, then it suggests it is part of best/recommended practices. However, this is clearly not enough in practice, and I think making the tool stricter overall (e.g., recommending reporting the whole model specification)can really push forward practices and make sure people report things more thoroughly.
I’m not sure if questions as formulated can 1. sufficiently discriminate between meta-analyses (for example, those that conduct a thorough publication bias analysis versus those that do it quickly) 2. Allow judgment of methodological reproducibility (for this, we need more details on the models; there are no questions on the number of databases used, the search string, …).
NA
Perhaps include an item evaluating if a Quality Assessment was undertaken. Item 2 or in the Glossary: provide a list of GUI softwares. Item 7: I would suggest also to include confidence intervals, or relative weight. Item 9: I would suggest also to include the respective lower and upper confidence intervals. Item 14: Sometimes although the extracted raw data is not reported, the authors describe the types of variables they extracted. Consider YES, even when the previous item was scored with a NO? In the glossary: pooled effect i.e., overall effect.
